code.description: This typed record declares exactly one condition - a capability the selected product requires that this release did not declare available - so its code is that condition, not any DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision referenced the whole enum and admitted CONFIG.INVALID on a release-absence notice.

Common1CapabilityAvailabilityNoticeV1.description: One capability the selected product requires that this release did not declare available, for ONE requested unit. The ownership tuple is carried in TYPED FIELDS - capabilityId, languageMode and the unit's own workspaceRoot - and is never concatenated into `subject`: workspaceRoot is a UserInputPath bounded at 4096 while BoundedText is 1024, so a concatenated subject could silently truncate a path and collapse two distinct requested units into one indistinguishable notice. Advisory: it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone Candidate.

Common1CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1.description: The availability account of ONE analysis step's own selection, associated with that step by stepId. `notices` is bounded at 1024 because that is the analysis-spec requestedCapabilities bound and one selection produces at most one absence per requested row, so a STEP's collection can never truncate and its noticeCount always equals its array length. The same ownership tuple may recur in different steps - two steps may select the same unit - so uniqueness is within a step, never across the invocation.

Common1CapabilityAvailabilityV1.description: The invocation's availability account, composed PER STEP. An earlier revision used one flat array bounded at 1024 and argued it could not truncate because that is the analysis-spec bound - but 1024 is per analysis-spec, not per invocation, and a named multi-step invocation carries up to 64 steps: two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices and the flat array refused. Composing per step preserves every valid admitted invocation: each step keeps its own bounded collection, `steps` is bounded by the invocation step bound (StepId 0..63), and no notice is ever discarded to fit. `totalNoticeCount` is the sum of the step counts and is authoritative for a caller counting absences across the invocation. A step that made no selection - a skipped step, or a non-analysis step - contributes NO entry; a step that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an empty array, which is the positive statement that it checked. A retried step keeps ONE entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.

Common1D9Deficiency.description: The HOST TERMINATION deficiency vocabulary of the D9 exit contract, carried by a whole Run, analysis result or comparison step: AnalysisResult.deficiency / .secondaryDeficiencies, ComparisonStepResult.d9Deficiency and comparison-result. It is NOT the per-requirement native sufficiency vocabulary, and the two are deliberately different sets. Three members (convergence-exhausted, baseline-recipe-unsupported, query-completeness-unmet) belong to evaluation, baseline and query outcomes that no per-requirement sufficiency evaluation can produce; `none` is the whole-Run `nothing was deficient` state, which a per-requirement record expresses by satisfied=true and the absence of the field. Four native sufficiency outcomes (derivation-policy-unmet, external-consumers-unknown, input-closure-incomplete, resolution-incomplete) have NO member here at all: they project outward as their own DomainDetailCode members and as the D9 class `indeterminate` (3) with the existing error code, per native-evidence.md section 10. Widening this enum to carry them was refused: it would put per-requirement causes into a whole-Run vocabulary and would change the D9 exit contract. Use #/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency wherever the value is one requirement's own outcome. PROVENANCE: this ENUM is unchanged from the inherited D9 exit contract and no member was added, removed or reordered by any correction in this series. The DEFINITION BYTES of this $defs entry did change, because this description was added; an earlier handoff said the definition was byte-unchanged, which was true only of the enum.

Common1D9FaultCause.description: Which operational fault applies. `host-invariant` is the successor member and its scope is narrow: the closed D9ErrorCode vocabulary already published SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE with no cause mapping to it, so the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically had no representable operational-failed termination, because that class requires BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause. Other host-fault causes - host-io, ledger-corrupt, provider-protocol and the rest - already existed and were always representable. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN, so an errorCode without a preimage was never a violation of totality, and this member does not `make the maps total`. It adds no error code, class, exit code or reason code, but it IS a vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one. The inherited docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json is HISTORICAL and unchanged, so its own enum still omits the member; the selected composition is native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-public-route-registry/hostInvariantSuccessor and publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit. Borrowing host-io for a host invariant violation is refused by contract: an I/O failure and an invariant violation are different remedies.

Common1ImportedRequirementDeficiency.description: The IMPORTED-EVIDENCE per-requirement outcome vocabulary, owned by imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law. An earlier revision used one flat array bounded at 1024 and argued it could not truncate because that is the analysis-spec bound - but 1024 is per analysis-spec, not per invocation, and a named multi-step invocation carries up to 64 steps: two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices and the flat array refused. Composing per step preserves every valid admitted invocation: each step keeps its own bounded collection, `steps` is bounded by the invocation step bound (StepId 0..63), and no notice is ever discarded to fit. `totalNoticeCount` is the sum of the step counts and is authoritative for a caller counting absences across the invocation. A step that made no selection - a skipped step, or a non-analysis step - contributes NO entry; a step that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an empty array, which is the positive statement that it checked. A retried step keeps ONE entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.

gating.description: Derived from admitted PolicyDocumentV2 enabled AND gate AND severity floor. Never inferred from ruleResults.outcome.

Common4CorrespondenceCoverage.description: Per-rule correspondence coverage, including zero-finding rules. populationUnknown is semantic incomplete (unavailable inventory record or no-covering-program), not a fabricated unavailable outcome for a missing expected inventory pointer (that pointer absence is structural refusal owned by enumeration/composition admission).

Common4D9Deficiency.description: The HOST TERMINATION deficiency vocabulary of the D9 exit contract, carried by a whole Run, analysis result or comparison step: AnalysisResult.deficiency / .secondaryDeficiencies, ComparisonStepResult.d9Deficiency and comparison-result. It is NOT the per-requirement native sufficiency vocabulary, and the two are deliberately different sets. Three members (convergence-exhausted, baseline-recipe-unsupported, query-completeness-unmet) belong to evaluation, baseline and query outcomes that no per-requirement sufficiency evaluation can produce; `none` is the whole-Run `nothing was deficient` state, which a per-requirement record expresses by satisfied=true and the absence of the field. Four native sufficiency outcomes (derivation-policy-unmet, external-consumers-unknown, input-closure-incomplete, resolution-incomplete) have NO member here at all: they project outward as their own DomainDetailCode members and as the D9 class `indeterminate` (3) with the existing error code, per native-evidence.md section 10. Widening this enum to carry them was refused: it would put per-requirement causes into a whole-Run vocabulary and would change the D9 exit contract. Use #/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency wherever the value is one requirement's own outcome. PROVENANCE: this ENUM is unchanged from the inherited D9 exit contract and no member was added, removed or reordered by any correction in this series. The DEFINITION BYTES of this $defs entry did change, because this description was added; an earlier handoff said the definition was byte-unchanged, which was true only of the enum.

Common4D9FaultCause.description: Which operational fault applies. `host-invariant` is the successor member and its scope is narrow: the closed D9ErrorCode vocabulary already published SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE with no cause mapping to it, so the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically had no representable operational-failed termination, because that class requires BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause. Other host-fault causes - host-io, ledger-corrupt, provider-protocol and the rest - already existed and were always representable. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN, so an errorCode without a preimage was never a violation of totality, and this member does not `make the maps total`. It adds no error code, class, exit code or reason code, but it IS a vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one. The inherited docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json is HISTORICAL and unchanged, so its own enum still omits the member; the selected composition is native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-public-route-registry/hostInvariantSuccessor and publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit. Borrowing host-io for a host invariant violation is refused by contract: an I/O failure and an invariant violation are different remedies.

Common4DomainDetailCode.description: Generated/drift-checked from docs/coop/design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json plus isolated evaluator3 members. Every owner joins the same closed registry; unknown names refuse. These details do not create D9 codes. Isolated additions: BASELINE.ENTRY_PROJECTION_CONFLICT, COMPARISON.CORRESPONDENCE_INCOMPLETE, EVALUATION.FINDING_JOIN_REFUSED, EVALUATION.MIXED_OUTPUT_MAJOR, EVALUATION.OUTPUT_BOUND_EXCEEDED, EVALUATION.PROOF_VERDICT_INCONSISTENT, EVALUATION.PROJECTION_INPUT_INCOMPLETE, EVALUATION.WORK_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, QUERY.CURSOR_MISMATCH, QUERY.ENDPOINT_AMBIGUOUS, QUERY.ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN, QUERY.FACT_VIEW_UNAVAILABLE, QUERY.PARAMS_MALFORMED, QUERY.RELATION_UNSUPPORTED, QUERY.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED, QUERY.VIEW_AMBIGUOUS, QUERY.VIEW_UNKNOWN, REPAIR.TARGET_CORRESPONDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, REPAIR.TARGET_METADATA_AMBIGUOUS. Shared registry members this surface must preserve (root registers in both common enums): EVALUATION.INPUT_REFUSED (structural evaluator input failure with the exact diagnostic retained separately), EVALUATION.SELECTION_LIMIT (well-formed prospective request above the published bound), EVALUATION.REQUIRED_OUTPUT_OMITTED (missing required provider or host output pointer on the public surface, retaining its exact reference). Do not fork a second registration. CONFIG.INVALID is a D9ErrorCode and a DomainDetailCode; it is not an arbitrary DomainDetail for evaluator3 join/projection refusals. Root integrates. Output bound error is existing D9ErrorCode OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED with faultCause output-serialization, never HOST.IO_FAILURE.

The reference model's values are SYNTHETIC fixture labels (see workflows_model.synthetic_execution_id) and are not a recipe. Braces and brackets are literal; no escape syntax. Candidate admission remains owned by its field.

Common4ImportedRequirementDeficiency.description: The IMPORTED-EVIDENCE per-requirement outcome vocabulary, owned by imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law. It applies to a repair EvidenceRequirement whose relation is `runtime-observation` or `history-change` - relations that mint no fact2, carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse and have no Coverage entry, so native section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2` cannot produce an outcome for them and is not asked to. Every member is bound to the payload field that grounds it, and EACH KIND REPORTS ONLY ITS OWN: a runtime requirement is projected through observability, observationWindow and observedPopulation; a history requirement through revisionRange and collectionScope, which are its BOUNDS fields - HistoryPayloadV1 has others, notably its subjects, but it carries no observationWindow, observedPopulation or observability at all. A satisfied imported requirement means the condition was met over the BOUND window or range - not that the evidence is positive: `observed-hit` is positive execution evidence and `observable-unhit` is bounded NEGATIVE evidence, and the disclosure records which satisfied it. No imported observation establishes a universal negative, and imported evidence can never BY ITSELF establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe delete or replace - though it may be an additional required condition alongside an already-established native basis.

Common4LogicalPath.description: Strict sealed logical path: relative, slash-separated, no empty/dot/dot-dot/NUL/backslash segments, each segment at most 255 bytes-as-characters. Used for snapshot inventories, edits, archive members, cwd and every identity-bearing path. Never a user-typed OS path.

Common4NativeSufficiencyDeficiency.description: The NATIVE PER-REQUIREMENT sufficiency outcome vocabulary: the exact nine members of DeficiencyV2, whose only defined producer is native-evidence.md section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2`, evaluated once per requirement. A record carrying one requirement's own outcome carries THIS vocabulary and never D9Deficiency, because four of these nine members have no D9Deficiency preimage and the D9-mapped value for all four is the same `verdict-indeterminate`, which would collapse exactly the distinction native-evidence.md section 10 preserves per row - including `resolution-incomplete`, the outcome section 4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal negative under unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid over an affected target, and the outcome a destructive unused-code repair recipe turns on. This record-level vocabulary is orthogonal to two other things and replaces neither: the PUBLIC D9 TERMINATION of the Run that carries the requirement (still #/$defs/D9Deficiency and the section 10 class/code columns), and the retained CAUSE CARRIER of the Coverage entry the outcome was read from (still entry.nativeCause or the named structured carrier, per the native deficiency-cause registry). `none` is deliberately absent: a satisfied requirement is satisfied=true with the field omitted, which is what sufficiency_v2 returns.

Common4NullableFingerprint.description: Matched findings carry finding-key2. Unmatched findings MUST be JSON null, never a surrogate or a run2/finding2 prefix.

Common4PinnedPurgeDisclosure.description: Complete current pin inventory observed under the purge writer lease. Operational pinId is a host-ledger name scoped to this Run, not a content identity or authority token. Never truncate this disclosure or infer destructive consent from it.

Common4RepairAuthorizationRef.description: Exact product H(security.repair-apply-authorization.v1, admitted RepairApplyAuthorizationV1) with the security.repair-apply-authorization.v1 prefix; current host admission is mandatory.

Common4SourceCorrespondence.description: Mandatory correspondence of external evidence to analyzed source. exact-snapshot binds a snapshot2 and is the only correspondence that is mapped by itself. vcs-revision binds a commit plus dirty flag and optional build identity; a commit string (even clean) or a declared build identity is a STATEMENT and cannot prove which generated/runtime bytes correspond to which snapshot bytes, so vcs-revision evidence is consumable only when an admitted SourceMappingV1 (imported-evidence schema) joins every consumed generated path to a snapshot2 inventory entry by digest; otherwise it is unmapped-only. The wrapper's sourceCorrespondenceDigest is the raw SHA-256 of this record's canonical bytes, retained as a blob.

sourceMappingDigest.description: raw SHA-256 of the canonical SourceMappingV1 bytes admitted with this evidence, or null when none was supplied (then vcs-revision evidence is unmapped-only)

Common4StepTermination.description: D9-shaped per-step or aggregate termination. exitCode is never stored; it derives from class by the fixed table (0,1,2,3,4,130). Branch contract: success carries no errorCode/reasonCodes/signal; policy-failed requires runId, or authority=ephemeral when the failing analysis was explicitly non-authoritative and therefore has no Run; request-rejected and operational-failed require errorCode (operational-failed also a non-none faultCause); indeterminate requires reasonCodes; interrupted requires signal and may carry runId only when a Run was committed before the interrupt. Retained D9 class/code legality (X1, X3, X4 and codeDerivation) is schema-enforced on the same branches: faultCause appears only on operational-failed and pairs with errorCode exactly as the fault map (D9 codeMaps.faultCauseToErrorCode plus the successor host-invariant member); reasonCodes appear only on indeterminate. Required-delivery detail law: DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT names a failure after this invocation committed a Run and requires that runId; DELIVERY.REQUIRED_PROJECTION_FAILED names a required projection or renderer failure when no Run was committed and forbids runId. Both are operational-failed / DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED; every other operational-failed termination keeps its existing optional runId.

Common4SubjectId.description: Opaque subject3 identity. Workflow projection must not unpack universe/kind/nativeId. Path for waiver, baseline subjectPath and repair metadata is finding.subject.logicalPath. For packages that path is the package manifest path (package names may repeat).

Common4UnmatchedOccurrence.description: Retained unmatched finding metadata. Excluded from fingerprint-keyed baseline entries. side is baseline or current. Historical schemaMajor 1 artifacts do not acquire an empty array assertion.

Common4UserInputPath.description: A user-named OS path (baseline file, import artifact, output file). Opened only through the security unit's nofollow/ACL custody; never enters any content identity; recorded in operational records only.

Comparison2AuditProfile.description: Explicit, visible gate semantics. code-regression (default for audit): gates CODE-NET-NEW on rules gating under baseline OR current policy; a new waiver added in the same change does not suppress it. policy-change: additionally gates findings newly live through POLICY/SCOPE/WAIVER deltas (used to review a policy change; code regressions still gate). full-current: every live unwaived gating finding on the current side gates, whatever its axis. report-only: nothing gates; verdict is pass or indeterminate only.

pivotsAvailable.description: Derived from what was actually bound, never assumed: E0 from the detector dispositions; E1..E3 are 'available' only when the current side supplied a bound re-evaluation result for that pivot (boundPivots), 'not-needed' when that axis is unchanged, else 'unavailable' (every entry INDETERMINATE pivot-reevaluation-unavailable).

ruleDeficiencies.description: sorted by ruleId; a gating deficiency yields verdict indeterminate even with zero entries

entries.description: sorted strictly ascending by fingerprint UTF-8 bytes

unmatchedOccurrences.description: Union of baseline and current unmatched findings. Not comparison entries and not classified as UNCHANGED, CODE-NET-NEW, or CODE-FIXED.

currentEvaluationState.description: Admitted current proof evaluationState. Independent of rule gating.

currentExecutionDeficiencies.description: Exact current proof executionDeficiencies (source-specific causes). Not collapsed into ruleDeficiencies. Execution unknown is independent of policy gating; matched CODE-NET-NEW fail still dominates.

currentClosureId.description: null when the current detector was removed, including indeterminate removal without an admitted pivot.

method.description: Identical or explicitly compatible closures permit two-way comparison. Changed or removed baseline detectors require a committed current-trusted E0 pivot over current source; removal sets E1..E4 false but preserves measured E0. New detectors set E0 false. Missing pivot is indeterminate; removal cannot hide code regressions.

subsequentDeltas.description: axes after the classifying axis at which presence/waiver status changed again; a CODE-NET-NEW entry with subsequentDeltas [policy] is a code regression hidden by a policy change and still gates

liveInCurrent.description: true only when E4 is a known hit and the current occurrence is not waived

gateReason.description: code-net-new-policy-hidden: a gating CODE-NET-NEW entry that is not live in current because a later axis hid it (a detector, policy or scope change, or a waiver added in the same change); subsequentDeltas names the later axes.

Comparison2EvaluationContext.description: Digests of the evaluation context on one side. policyDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical PolicyDocumentV1 bytes (equals plan.policyDigest); waiverSetDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical RESOLVED WaiverSetV1 bytes (equals plan.waiverDigest); scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical ScopeDocumentV1 bytes (the workflow glob scope-policy document, bound as an analysis-spec parameter; distinct from plan.scopeDigest, which is the foundation scope-descriptor). All three are retained blobs. detectorClosureIds are closure2 identities. evidenceAvailability lists the exact imports, kinds and required relations actually bound on that side.

Comparison2EvidenceAvailability.description: Evidence actually bound on one side. imports lists the exact import2 identities (each already binds payload content, correspondence, scope and observation digests) so that the evidence axis compares identities, not kind presence: the same kind with different payload/correspondence/scope/window is a changed axis. importKinds is derived from imports and retained for the rule evidenceUse join.

Comparison2ExecutionDeficiency.description: Drift-checked copy of foundation3 evaluation-deficiency required fields. Full Run replay is a prerequisite. Not a Comparison RuleDeficiency cause key.

Comparison2PivotPresence.description: Presence knowledge of the fingerprint at each pivot. true = a known matched occurrence (waived included). false = non-selection (that side's policy does not enable the rule or its ScopeDocument does not select the path; attributed to the policy or scope axis, never CODE-FIXED) or evaluated absence proved by that side's rule under the complete-hit-set law (enabled rule, evaluated, complete enumeration, every selected emitWhen root determinate, fingerprint absent from the emitted matched set, path inside the attested extent, no unmatched occurrence at that side that might be the fingerprint). null = not known. No fingerprint is minted for an unmatched occurrence. B is evaluated-absent only when the baseline RuleCoverage absenceKnowledge is complete-hit-set. waivedB/waivedC record waiver status on the two real sides.

Comparison2Root.title: ComparisonResult schemaMajor 2 — evaluator3 unmatched + correspondence coverage
Comparison2Root.description: Explicit successor to versioning-policy.v8.json#comparisonSchema.ComparisonResult. Attribution follows a fixed pivot chain over CURRENT source: E0 = (prior detector, prior policy, prior scope, prior waivers); E1 = (current detector, prior policy/scope/waivers); E2 = (current detector, current policy, prior scope/waivers); E3 = (current detector/policy/scope, prior waivers); E4 = current Run. Baseline B is the artifact's entry set. Each entry's classification is the FIRST axis in the order code→detection→policy→scope→waiver at which its presence (or waived status, for the waiver axis) changes, and later axes are recorded in subsequentDeltas, so a code regression cannot be hidden under a simultaneous policy, scope, waiver or evidence change. E1..E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current facts under the baseline's embedded context documents (fresh CI needs no origin store). E0 requires a runnable admitted prior detector closure; when it is unavailable and the detector changed without a declared exact semantic compatibility, every entry of that detector is INDETERMINATE with a typed reason. Gate semantics are selected by the named audit profile, never by enum precedence. Whole-comparison indeterminacy performs no comparison and emits zero entries. Evaluator3: schemaMajor 2 because unmatchedOccurrences and correspondenceCoverage are identity-bearing. Unmatched records are not classified as UNCHANGED, CODE-NET-NEW, CODE-FIXED or resolved. Known matched CODE-NET-NEW still fails even when gating correspondence deficiencies exist. Historical schemaMajor 1 is refused, never coerced to empty unmatched.

gating.description: true when the rule's effective severity under this side's policy fails the gate

absenceKnowledge.description: complete-hit-set when this side can prove absence of a non-emitted fingerprint of the rule: enabled, not budget-exhausted, outcome not indeterminate, complete enumeration and every selected emitWhen root determinate. Otherwise unknown (including disabled rules). Independent of requiredCoverage.

Comparison2RuleDeficiency.description: Current-side rule deficiency independent of classified matched entries. correspondence-incomplete covers unmatched findings and semantic population unknown (unavailable inventory record or no-covering-program) including zero-finding rules. A missing expected inventory POINTER is not this cause: that is structural admission refusal.

value.description: The deterministic analysis budget. identity-and-evidence section 3 requires plan.budget to equal this value exactly and by type; an override is made here first so both committed places agree.

Detector1Root.title: DetectorManifestV1 — unsigned compatibility listing at reserved closure.tree path

Graph3Root.description: Every query names one ProjectId and exactly one view selector. The 20 operation names are unchanged. Parameters are closed per operation. Non-graph snapshot metadata operations keep request View on the response and MUST NOT be forced to run-only. Bounds (schema constants, not request fields): page size 1..1000 (default 100); at most 100000 items per logical operation; traversal depth at most 64; at most 1000000 visited nodes. Work bounds apply across the logical operation and do not reset per page. A bound reached under completeness=required is QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET (indeterminate); under best-effort it is truncated-bound with no continuation past the cap. Queries never materialise facts, invoke a provider, allocate an attempt, seal a Run, derive policy or choose termination. Advisory is cross-joined: true exactly for AdvisoryOperation members, false for graph.* and the remaining non-advisory operations. Evaluator3 schemaMajor 3. params.findingId locates unmatched and matched findings on finding ops. params.fingerprint locates matched occurrences only. RunId is run3. Native/input prefixes stay snapshot2/plan2/closure2/import2/fact2/view2. No global database id and no FactViewId recipe.

Not a 64-hex field of this bundle and deliberately not annotated as one: it is an owner-admitted identity carried inside a derived record, joined by equality to the retained context and never re-hashed here. Its width differs by language by construction.

oneOf.description: The dialect axis of a GRAMMAR-ONLY interpretation; used only by the syntax-only universe. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so it has no edition to select and no tsconfig program to join. Claiming an edition for a .rs body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics, and reusing sourceVariant would let a grammar-parsed body carry the identical dialect token as a compiler-parsed one. The token is the variant the bundled grammar selects from the body's own suffix. Because this is a DIFFERENT branch, a syntax-only body identity can never collide with a compiler-derived identity over the same bytes - which is the intended distinction, not a defect: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different interpretations of the span and equating them would be a false clone claim.

dialect.description: The SELECTED source-language dialect of the body being identified: the edition of its owning compilation unit, the source variant its own suffix denotes, or - for a grammar-only interpretation - the grammar variant that suffix selects. Never a whole map and never null - a language with no declared dialect axis would be an unexamined default, and there is none. Including a map would make one body identity depend on unrelated crates and would not be representable inside the inherited u8 component length.

Identity3CommitInventory.description: The closed record digested by commit-receipt.inventoryDigest: the exact set of typed object identities and retained raw blob digests the commit published for this Run.

Identity3Domain.description: Registered digest-domain name. This enumeration and #/$defs/Ref/properties/domain are the same set, and both are the registered keys of x-opensip-digest-domains.byDomain.

oneOf.description: The typed cause carried beside a DeficiencyV2 in a Coverage entry. The three body-language-* members are the clones ownership states that identity-and-evidence and native-evidence section 11 require the clones Coverage to DISCLOSE: the contract mandates that such a scope mint no body identity, that its Coverage report the incompleteness, and that the predicate and seal be indeterminate rather than a false pass -- and until these members existed no value in this closed vocabulary could name why. A nullable nativeCause does not satisfy a mandated disclosure; a null there records that a disclosure was owed and not made. The other selectionLaw causes deliberately have NO member here: BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED and BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED are per-body refusals that section 11 states are compatible with coverage=complete (the host examined that subject and correctly produced no fact for it), and BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT/BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS are universe-level dialect faults that refuse before any Coverage entry is minted.

Identity3EvaluationDeficiency.description: Closed replayed deficiency with explicit origin. evidenceKind is data provenance bound to the policy atom/declaration, not a gating flag. Native carrier, universe, subject, predicate and inputRefs are rederived from admitted inputs per composition §9.5–§9.6. Execution-assessment items use source=execution and inputRefs = ExecutionInputsV1 ref plus originating row refs. Atom items on a native/import plane copy evaluationInputRefs except Coverage-entry items which name that Coverage.

Identity3EvaluationSubject.description: Configuration-qualified subject. File/symbol native IDs are unique in kind/universe. Package names can repeat at different first-party manifests, so packageManifestPath is a required package-only coordinate. No synthetic native package spelling or encounter-order suffix.

outputDomains.description: Declared output-domain set. Empty is permitted and asserts no output domains; it does not establish completeness or result authority. Stage and stage-spec sets must agree.

evidenceRefs.description: Root predicate-witness digest; descendant known and uncertain facts; descendant witness coverageIds (consulted); descendant matching/uncertain observation importIds; and every evaluationInputRefs member with domain=import. Enumeration/execution inventory refs stay on the proof. composition §9.7.

Identity3Finding.description: Version3 finding: one full configuration-qualified occurrence. subjectId is evaluation-subject; fingerprint is unchanged logical correspondence. Baseline projection groups only identical logical fingerprint descriptors and complete BaselineEntry fields.

Identity3FindingParameters.description: The closed record digested by finding.parameterDigest. parameters is an object map so that parameter names are unique and ordered by the canonical encoder itself, with no ordering annotation to elect.

blobs.description: The closed inventory of the import's retained AUXILIARY ASSET members. It is not the import's mandatory custody: the payload bytes and the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes are retained and re-hashed independently by registered_payload, and those obligations hold identically when this array is empty. An archive member outside this list is never read (native-evidence section 3 PO-4) - a restriction on READING, satisfied vacuously by an empty list, never a requirement that a member exist. minItems 0 is therefore the owning admissibility: a self-contained normalized payload may legitimately retain no auxiliary asset. An earlier revision of this description required minItems 1, arguing that adapterClosure asserts an adapter ran over the bytes named by the custody record's sourcePath; that argument was withdrawn because ImportedEvidenceRecordV1.sourcePath is a UserInputPath, which the workflow common schema defines as never entering any content identity and recorded in operational records only, and because no join anywhere binds sourcePath to a member of this array. Requiring one arbitrary blob would not establish original-input custody. maxItems 4096 and the item byte bound are the import unit's own published hostile-input bounds (workflows/schemas/imported-evidence.schema.json top-level description: at most 4096 blobs, artifact at most 268435456 bytes); the foundation record previously allowed 100000, and narrowing to the published bound is a stated compatibility change.

Identity3ImportBlob.description: A retained blob row of an import. Identical to Blob except for the import unit's own published hostile-input artifact bound (imported-evidence.schema.json: 'artifact at most 268435456 bytes'), which is an import bound and deliberately not imposed on source-inventory or closure tree rows. Exact mirror of workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/Blob.

Identity3ImportObservationAddress.description: Exact row address within the payload selected by importId. execution selects the TestPayload as a whole; other selectors select subjects[ordinal] or tests[ordinal]. Owner admission checks kind/selector, bounds and explicit Plan/evaluation-input membership. This new descriptor is inline in its witness and is not assigned fragment retention.

Identity3LogicalPath.description: The logical-path grammar identity-and-evidence section 3 already states: relative, slash-separated, no empty/dot/dot-dot/NUL/backslash segment, each segment at most 255 characters. THREE DIFFERENT ENFORCEMENTS EXIST AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT; this description states only where each applies and changes no accepted path set. (1) DIRECT $ref, exactly two fields: #/$defs/Blob/properties/path and #/$defs/import-blob/properties/path. Only these carry the full declarative grammar, INCLUDING the at-most-255-characters-per-segment bound. (2) fact/anchors[]/path: a plain bounded string here, additionally subject to the imperative recursive check in foundation/identity-model.py `ordered()` AND to a real snapshot JOIN - an anchor path must be an inventoried snapshot path, and inventory rows ARE Blob, so the declarative grammar reaches it through that join. (3) finding-fingerprint/subjectKey/logicalPath: a plain bounded string subject to the SAME imperative `ordered()` check and to NO snapshot join. `ordered()` refuses, for any string under a key named `path` or `logicalPath` at any depth, a leading slash, a backslash, a NUL and any empty/dot/dot-dot segment - and it does NOT enforce the per-segment 255 maximum. So (3) is not equivalently constrained to (1), and no snapshot join is claimed for it. The three scope-descriptor path arrays deliberately reference none of this, because `.` alone denotes the admitted project root and this grammar forbids a dot segment. Byte-identical in constraint to workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/LogicalPath, which is what makes the import blob rows an exact mirror.

Identity3NormalizationSpecificationMap.description: The per-level normalization specification map a body-interpreting closure publishes (x-opensip-digest-domains.normalizationSpecificationLaw). Its canonical bytes C(this) are the closure tree member at the law's closureTreePath; each row names the exact retained level-specification bytes for one normalisation level. levels is strictly ascending by the UTF-8 bytes of level, so one map has one spelling.

levels.description: Strictly ascending by the UTF-8 bytes of level; enforced at Run closure (BODY_NORMALIZATION_MAP_INVALID).

Identity3OwnerSourceSet.description: The closed record digested by semantic-grant.principals[].ownerSourceDigest: the security contract RepoExecutionGrantV2 owner projection, strictly ascending and unique by ownerKey UTF-8 bytes.

semanticClosures.description: Explicit selection with required membership under x-opensip-digest-domains.closureMembership, not an exact minimal set. Extra admissible retained closures may be selected; their selection changes PlanId.

budget.description: Equal, exactly and by type, to the analysis.budget of the committed resolved semantic configuration this Plan names (identity-and-evidence section 3 closure list). A legitimate override enters the resolved configuration first; neither committed place silently wins.

Identity3PredicateWitness.description: Version3 witness. No inputRefs field: the complete admitted evaluation input selection is projected onto predicateProofs[].inputRefs (composition §9.2). Native atoms carry native matches/uncertain matches and Coverage; imported atoms carry observation addresses, never fact2; boolean nodes carry children and empty match/Coverage arrays. coverageIds and matching/uncertain sets are consulted evidence and may be narrower than evaluationInputRefs. Exact source-specific plane/operation constraints and complete replay are evaluator admission laws.

Identity3ProgramPredicate.description: The closed record digested by predicate-witness.programPredicateDigest. It addresses ONE predicate node of the admitted RuleProgramV2; it introduces no second policy language. predicateId is the node address: the rule root is "p", the i-th operand of an and/or node at address a is a+"."+i (zero-based, shortest decimal), and the operand of a not node at address a is a+".0".

ruleProgramDigest.description: equal to the proof bundle ruleProgramDigest this witness belongs to

nodeDigest.description: raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the exact predicate node the rule program carries at rules[ruleId].emitWhen addressed by predicateId; its op equals operation

evaluationInputRefs.description: Complete admitted selection: ExecutionInputsV1.selectedRefs plus the one execution-inputs ref. Not an evaluated subset. Atomic predicateProofs[].inputRefs copy this whole set (composition §9.2).

inputRefs.description: Atomic: equal to proof.evaluationInputRefs (whole admitted selection, including empty-population inputs). Boolean: canonical union of immediate children. Projection of the witness-binding sentence; witnesses have no inputRefs field. Not the atom internal consumed-ref subset. composition §9.2.

executionDeficiencies.description: Required-execution assessment items even when all rules are disabled, plus work-budget-exhausted. source=execution is the assessment layer. cause is row.deficiency if it is an execution-registry member, else required-cell-unsatisfied for null/source-syntax-invalid. inputRefs are the ExecutionInputsV1 ref plus originating Coverage/inventory/candidate refs. subjectId and predicateId are null. composition §9.6. Internal requiredCellDeficiencies tokens native-work-incomplete/unsupported-typed are not proof causes.

Identity3ProofBundle.description: Version3 COMPLETE normalized evaluator output. Rule enumerations/results, all predicate proofs/witnesses, full findings and waiver membership, execution deficiencies and sealed verdict are independently recomputed. Count-only comparison is not replay. A deterministic preflight budget refusal is explicit and never an empty successful analysis.

Identity3RuleEnumeration.description: Retained OUTPUT recomputed from Plan-bound expected inventories and rule selection. Incomplete includes unavailable and partial population or unknown export membership. Complete-empty is explicit. Disabled is all arrays empty. Inventory refs include all relevant expected outcomes, including unavailable records; unseen population never gets a fabricated subject id.

Identity3RuleResult.description: One result for EVERY compiled policy rule, including disabled and zero-subject rules, strictly sorted by ruleId. Outcome is recomputed after explicit waiver resolution and effective gate selection; advisory matches remain findings with pass sealed rule outcome. Enumeration uncertainty survives waived known findings.

budget.description: The deterministic analysis budget. identity-and-evidence section 3 requires plan.budget to equal this value exactly and by type; an override is made here first so both committed places agree.

importIds.description: Exactly the Plan-selected import set of this Run's Plan, repeated: equal as a canonical set to plan.importIds (IMPORT_JOIN). A repetition of the selection, never a second selection. This array is not an evaluated subset and is not proof.evaluationInputRefs (that field is the complete selectedRefs plus the execution-inputs ref). A selected import that nothing evaluated is still resolved and retained by the Run closure, and being selected alone grants it no evidence authority. Matched and uncertain observation addresses live on predicate-witness matchingImportRows/uncertainImportRows. Atomic predicateProofs[].inputRefs copy the whole evaluationInputRefs under composition §9.2 and therefore may list every selected import without those imports being consulted observation evidence.

Identity3SourceInventory.description: The snapshot source inventory as a registered record in its own right, so that vcs-observation.sourceInventoryDigest names a record rather than an unnamed canonical fragment.

Identity3StageSpec.description: The closed record digested by stageSpecDigest. execution-plan.stages[].stageSpecDigest and cache-key.stageSpecDigest are the SAME field name because they are the same digest of the same record under the same recipe; there are not two recipes for one spelling.

parameters.description: every row must also be a row of the Plan analysis-spec parameters: a stage takes no hidden input

outputDomains.description: Declared output-domain set. Empty is permitted and asserts no output domains; it does not establish completeness or result authority. Stage and stage-spec sets must agree.

enumeratorClosure.description: The Plan-selected closure that enumerated this scope. Its kind must be 'provider': enumeration is a native provider act, and no 'enumerator' kind is minted for it. The closure must also be a member of plan.semanticClosures, so the enumerator is one the Plan selected.

Imported1BuildIdentityV1.description: Closed preimage of wrapper.buildDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob).

Imported1HistoryPayloadV1.description: Payload domain workflow.import-payload.history.v1. Advisory priority input only.

Imported1ImportObservationV1.description: Closed preimage of wrapper.observationDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob). Null members mean the observation semantics do not apply to the kind.

Imported1ImportScopeDescriptor.description: Exact mirror of foundation identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/scope-descriptor: the foundation record is the AUTHORITY and this document restates it field-for-field, including every array's owning x-opensip-order. wrapper.scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of this record (the same producing rule as plan.scopeDigest); retained as a blob. There is no separate workflow import-scope domain. Because one digest preimage is admitted through both documents, they must admit and refuse exactly the same bytes; the mirror-drift check proves it rather than asserting it.

Imported1ImportWrapperV2.description: Exact mirror of foundation import descriptor fields (schemaVersion 2). Every auxiliary digest is a raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an exact closed record retained as a blob (identity-and-evidence §2 auxiliary-digest rule); none is an H(domain) identity: payloadSchemaDigest = raw SHA-256 of the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes (PayloadRegistryV1 row); payloadDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes; sourceCorrespondenceDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical common#SourceCorrespondence; buildDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical BuildIdentityV1; scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportScopeDescriptor (= foundation scope-descriptor); observationDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportObservationV1. importId = 'import2:' + H('import', this object) is the only H-domain identity in an import. No hidden metadata: every field is one of these thirteen.

Imported1ImportedEvidenceRecordV1.description: Operational custody record joining the wrapper, its payload binding, the resolved correspondence and staleness for a given Plan. Only importId enters the Plan (plan.importIds).

Imported1PayloadBinding.description: Closed table row: which registered payload schema each import kind admits and which contract owns the payload semantics.

payloadDomain.description: ONE registry, five rows: runtime/test/history admit ONLY the workflow payload domains (native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history adapter grammars are normalized by native into these payloads BEFORE import and are not import payload domains); dependency/prepared admit ONLY native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1 / native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1 (native-evidence.md §7 spellings).

schemaDocument.description: the registered schema DOCUMENT whose exact complete bytes hash to payloadSchemaDigest (raw SHA-256 of the file bytes; no canonical-schema hash exists)

selector.description: JSON pointer of the payload $def inside schemaDocument; the selector identifies the definition, the digest binds the document bytes

Imported1PayloadRegistryV1.description: The one closed import payload registry. Exactly these five rows exist; any other (kind, payloadDomain) pair is IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH and a domain with no row is IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED.

Imported1Root.title: Imported evidence: one foundation import2 wrapper, typed payloads as content (PROPOSED, revised)
Imported1Root.description: Import is an operational admission step (import custody), never an analysis Run. There is exactly ONE import identity: importId = H('import', foundation import descriptor) from foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import (schemaVersion 2). The typed payload records here (runtime, test, history) and native's typed records (dependency-source, prepared-output, and native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history payload grammars) are PAYLOADS: their bytes are referenced by payloadDigest (raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes) and their registered schema by payloadSchemaDigest. The wrapper's identity therefore differs from the payload content hash, and one payload can appear under two wrappers only if correspondence/producer/adapter/scope also agree, which is the intended meaning. Hostile-input bounds: artifact at most 268435456 bytes; at most 1048576 subjects; at most 4096 blobs; JSON depth at most 32; strict UTF-8, no duplicate keys, no float lexemes, no surrogates. Observed no-hits during one window are never universal non-use; only observable-unhit subjects may be consumed by a predicate, and only with the window/population disclosed.

Imported1RuntimePayloadV1.description: Payload domain workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1. Its raw canonical bytes hash to wrapper.payloadDigest.

subjects.description: sorted strictly ascending by (path, symbol) UTF-8 bytes

observability.description: unobservable: the capture could not observe this subject (no source map, not instrumented); unmapped: no correspondence to an inventoried source path. Neither is ever an unhit signal.

Imported1SourceMappingV1.description: The one closed mapping artifact that makes vcs-revision/declared-build evidence consumable. Producing recipe: the adapter that generated the runtime/test artifact emits, for every generated path it observed, the digest of the generated bytes and the digest and path of the snapshot source it was built from; the host admits the mapping only when every sourceSha256 equals the snapshot2 inventory digest of sourcePath (else IMPORT.SOURCE_MAPPING_REQUIRED and the evidence stays unmapped-only). Digest: raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, retained as a blob and carried in SourceCorrespondence.sourceMappingDigest.

entries.description: sorted ascending by generatedPath; generatedPath unique

Imported1StalenessRule.description: Closed decision table row for staleness classification relative to a Plan's snapshot binding.

verdictGate.description: Step gate participation. self (default when absent): the Run verdict terminates this step (fail → policy-failed). delegated: this analysis supplies the current Run to exactly one later comparison step (which must name it as currentStep); its Run verdict does NOT terminate the step — completion, operational faults and requiredCoverage≠satisfied / verdict=indeterminate still do. Invocation3AnalysisResult.description: Closed union. authoritative: a committed Run with receipt. ephemeral: no Run, no receipt, no authority; carries only semantic plan/evidence identities so that a result can be cited, and can never satisfy baseline adoption, repair preconditions, or verify.

installationJournalRefs.description: Installation mutation attempts only. Initial attempt: first LEASED after all locks, then durable revisions written in order. Recovery attempt: first is the observed installationRecoveryStartRef (any closed state), then revisions written by this attempt. Earlier attempt records remain unchanged. Required once a journal exists, including failed/abandoned attempts; absent before any journal. Operational custody, excluded from Run identity.

installationRecoveryStartRef.description: Recovery attempt only: exact current durable revision read under the installation fence; equals installationJournalRefs[0]. It is host-observed, never accepted from request input.

Invocation3BaselineInspectRequestV1.description: baseline show [PATH]: the tracked baseline artifact path (default opensip.baseline.json resolved by the host).

phase.description: before-settle: at least one required step had not reached a terminal outcome; aggregate is interrupted (130). after-settle: every required step already reached a terminal outcome; the aggregate termination is not reclassified.

currentStep.description: the authoritative primary analysis whose Run is the current side; that step must carry verdictGate=delegated and must be in dependsOn

pivotStep.description: the role=pivot analysis step when E0 is needed; must be in dependsOn

Invocation3ComparisonStepResult.description: Operational projection of a ComparisonResultV1. The step termination is derived from verdict: fail → policy-failed (runId = currentRunId); indeterminate → indeterminate with reasonCodes [VERDICT.INDETERMINATE] or [BASELINE.RECIPE_UNSUPPORTED] per d9Deficiency and the descriptor remedy as domainDetail; pass → success (runId = currentRunId). Never defaults to success.

Invocation3CoreTransitionIntentV1.description: One closed installation intent for core update/repair/rollback and store migrate/rollback. Security S9.2 admits exact per-operation closure/schema/store/deadline semantics and journals the derived namespace lease set. Store operations keep the core closure; a same-schema core operation keeps the store. Target trust/profile/generation/time observations are host-admitted, never caller granted.

Invocation3DerivationBinding.description: Explicit mapping from one analysis/verify attempt to its derivation DAG. The workflow step DAG (≤64 steps) and the derivation DAG (≤1024 stages) are distinct: a step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. One attempt owns exactly one execution plan; a retry attempt on identical admitted inputs may bind the same exec-plan2 and Run.

Native2CanonicalRelativeDirV1.description:
INTERNAL relative DIRECTORY form: one or more slash-joined non-empty segments, no leading or trailing slash, no empty segment, no "." or ".." segment, no NUL and no backslash. Segments are decided by SPLITTING ON "/" and testing EXACT equality, which is the decision procedure the house already implements identically in two independent places: foundation/identity-model.v3.py `ordered()` (rejects a leading "/", a backslash, a NUL and any segment in ["", ".", ".."] for every `path`/`logicalPath` string) and discovery-defaults.py `normalize_explicit_root()` (same four tests over `spec.split("/")`). The negative test is therefore attached PER SEGMENT and ends with a strict end-of-input assertion rather than "$": "$" also matches before a trailing newline, and a ".*"-prefixed lookahead does not cross a newline at all, so a single whole-string lookahead both accepts "a
/../b" (an exact ".." segment) and rejects "a/.
" (whose final segment is ".
", not "."). No character beyond "/", backslash and NUL is excluded, because the owning grammar excludes none: a literal newline or other non-dot character inside a segment stays admissible. The declarative at-most-255-characters-per-segment bound of #/$defs/LogicalPath is deliberately NOT imported here; identity-schemas.v3 records it as a different, explicitly non-equivalent enforcement that reaches only two Blob path fields, and neither `ordered()` nor `normalize_explicit_root` imposes it. CanonicalPath is deliberately NOT this grammar: it admits a trailing slash and an interior empty segment ("a//b"), neither of which is canonical for a directory used as a membership prefix. The project root is NOT spelled here; see InternalUnitRootV1.

It is a raw artifact digest of a file, not an H identity, and it is NOT rust-v2.configProjectionSha256, which is the 64-hex suffix of H(native.cargo-config-projection.v2, CargoConfigProjectionV2) over this whole record (section 3.3).

Native2NativeCause.description: The typed cause carried beside a DeficiencyV2 in a Coverage entry. The three body-language-* members are the clones ownership states that identity-and-evidence and native-evidence section 11 require the clones Coverage to DISCLOSE: the contract mandates that such a scope mint no body identity, that its Coverage report the incompleteness, and that the predicate and seal be indeterminate rather than a false pass -- and until these members existed no value in this closed vocabulary could name why. A nullable nativeCause does not satisfy a mandated disclosure; a null there records that a disclosure was owed and not made. The other selectionLaw causes deliberately have NO member here: BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED and BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED are per-body refusals that section 11 states are compatible with coverage=complete (the host examined that subject and correctly produced no fact for it), and BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT/BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS are universe-level dialect faults that refuse before any Coverage entry is minted.

Native2ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1.description: The authenticated release declaration registry as a whole. Rows are unique; a duplicate capabilityId refuses rather than being merged, because two rows declaring different applicable modes for one capability would leave default selection ambiguous.

Native2ResolutionCompletenessState.description: Which member is legal on a given entry is decided by RC-1 (native-evidence.md section 4.3) and is NOT schema-decidable: applicability is total over the registered (relation, rung) pairs and turns on membership of the RUNG in the closed five-member resolved set (resolved-target, resolved-binding, resolved-callee, checked, from-resolved-calls), never on the relation ladder length. A resolved rung must never be not-applicable - reachability@from-resolved-calls is a one-rung relation whose single rung IS resolved - and every other registered rung, including unresolved-edge@observed and types@annotated as well as the syntactic rungs, is not-applicable with attempted=false, unresolvedEdgeCount=0 and unresolvedEdgeClasses=[]. RC-0 runs first and is relation-specific: the pair must be registered, meaning the rung is a member of THAT relation's own ladder, so unresolved-edge@enumerated is refused although both tokens are registered. That check and the not-applicable minting law (attempted false, count 0, empty class list) are enforced by coverage_bijection at the producer boundary AND again at retained Run closure, and they hold for a FACT-FREE entry over an empty examined scope. not-applicable is never a fallback for an unregistered pair. stageTerminal is deliberately not constrained: a not-applicable entry may retain the stage terminal its producer observed.

Native2ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1.description: The retained resolution read-set layout a TypeScript context commits to when nodeModulesInReadSet is true. One row per installed package DIRECTORY inside the project that the resolver may read: installPath is the project-relative directory as the resolver walks it, realPath is the project-relative directory after symlink/workspace-link resolution (equal to installPath when there is no link), and contentSha256 is the raw SHA-256 of that package directory manifest file bytes (its package.json) as RETAINED, joined by digest (the blobJoin on the native.context.typescript.v2 nested record, native-evidence section 2.2). A layout ROW is a package-directory resolution observation, not itself a snapshot inventory row. The FILES the analysis actually read inside a listed package directory ARE snapshot inventory rows (identity-and-evidence section 3 'What sourceInventory contains'; native-evidence section 1.4 U-4/U-4a): they have membership syntax-only / host-ignore-convention, are retained under their inventory digests, and Run closure joins each such row to the installPath or realPath of a row of this record, refusing SNAPSHOT_PRUNED_TREE_NOT_A_READ otherwise. Unread material in an installed dependency tree is never inventoried. This record commits package-directory granularity only: which files inside a listed package were read is a host TCB observation. Required inputs read from OUTSIDE the project root, such as compiler library files and the TypeScript standard library, stay in their owning toolchain and stdlib closures and are never snapshot paths. An earlier description said no inventory row could exist for files in these directories; that contradicted the selected read-set law and is superseded. Rows are strictly ascending and unique by installPath, so one layout has one spelling. nodeModulesLayoutDigest is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record); it is null exactly when nodeModulesInReadSet is false.

sourceUnitOwnershipId.description: Required and nullable, exactly as preparedOutputSetId is. null means NO committed ownership: such a universe admits no clones fact AT ALL, whatever its edition map looks like. An earlier revision of this description said null was admissible 'only while the edition map has a single distinct value, where every body has the same dialect and no owner selection arises'. That was the withdrawn package-default fast path and it is contradicted by the retained selectionLaw and by body_language_version, which refuses on missing ownership unconditionally: Cargo lets a target override its package default, so even a single-valued edition map can contain targets at different effective editions, and agreeing package defaults therefore never determine a body's dialect. The nullable form is retained deliberately - a universe whose ownership is unavailable or only partially enumerated is a legitimate retained universe; it simply mints no body identity, its clones Coverage carries the typed ownership disclosure (deficiency input-closure-incomplete with the matching body-language-* nativeCause), and its empty clone view stays indeterminate rather than becoming a finding of no clones.

Native2RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.description: executionCapableResolution=true means only that prepared products of some execution were consumed as inert data (preparedResolution != none). It is never a host execution grant; the grant is the operational RepoExecutionGrantV1 reference outside Plan.

Native2SourceUnitOwnershipV1.description: The committed relation from a SNAPSHOT SOURCE PATH to the compilation TARGET that reads it, the closed table of those targets, and the EXPLICIT SELECTION of which of them this universe analyses. It exists because a body span dialect is a property of the compilation target: neither a crate-name-to-root map nor the package edition map can supply it, since #[path], files shared by several targets and several compilation contexts of one crate defeat a directory inference, and Cargo lets a target override its package default edition. Because this record is committed by H identity inside RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId, a different SELECTION is a different record, a different identity and therefore a DIFFERENT sourceUniverse: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is validly analysed under each, one selection at a time, with no change to any relation payload. Every row is a retained native observation; nothing here executes Cargo, a build script or a repository read, and nothing here qualifies a compiler or an enumerator.

enumeration.description: complete: every compiled source path OF THE SELECTED UNITS has a row, so a path with no row is not compiled by any selected target. partial: the producer did not finish, so an owner INSIDE the selected scope may exist that is not listed. These are different claims and the second is not a weaker form of the first: an unlisted owner could contradict a listed one, so no clone body dialect is admissible under partial. That is checked BEFORE any row lookup, so partial discovery can never act as an implicit edition selection by hiding a conflicting owner. Partial evidence remains useful under the existing facts and Coverage law: the clones scope reports its incompleteness and the predicate is indeterminate, rather than a body identity being minted on an unbounded claim.

units.description: The closed table of compilation targets. Strictly unique by unitId, and unitId is a FUNCTION of the metadata, so two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal rather than two units that differ by accident. A selection or an ownership row naming a unitId with no row here is an unbound caller label and is inadmissible.

unitId.description: H(native.compilation-unit.v1, UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion:1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName}) over the very fields this row carries. DERIVED retention: nothing separate is retained because the preimage IS the row, and admission re-derives and compares (sourceUnitOwnership.unitId). Not an opaque digest - preimage record, domain and selector are all published - and not a delimiter label, which could stay injective only by narrowing admitted repository paths.

markerPath.description: The inventoried manifest that declares this target: the same markerPath vocabulary WorkspaceUnitV2 already uses, cited rather than duplicated. WorkspaceUnitV2 and UnitMembershipV1 identify WORKSPACE units - cargo-package and cargo-workspace - which is the wrong granularity here, because one package holds several targets that may carry different editions; naming the marker joins the two rather than competing with them.

crateName.description: A key of the universe edition map, which supplies the package default.

targetEdition.description: The target's OWN edition when it sets one, null when it takes the package default. Cargo documents edition on a target as well as on a package: cargo-metadata lists targets[].edition and states the package edition is a DEFAULT individual targets may differ from. null DEFERS to the universe edition map for crateName, so the two committed places can never contradict: an override is explicit and visible, and its absence is explicit too.

selectedUnitIds.description: The EXPLICIT analysis scope: the compilation targets this universe analyses. Every member must be a unitId of the units table. This is what makes a shared path representable at two editions without an ambiguous claim - two selections are two universes - and it is what distinguishes SELECTED SCOPE from INCOMPLETE ENUMERATION. An owner outside the selection is deliberately out of scope and its edition does not bear on a body; an unlisted owner INSIDE the selection is a gap in knowledge and refuses. Silently omitting a conflicting owner from the units table is not a selection: the omission is invisible, whereas a selection is committed in the identity.

ownership.description: The pure relation. It carries no edition and no metadata, so it cannot contradict the units table.

Native2SubjectScopeCommitmentV1.description: The producing result for the retained c2-plan-stage-schema.v4 coverage key field. subjectScopeCommitment is the SAME 64 hex as the foundation subject-scope identity scopeId, re-spelled in the native Sha256Text text form; it introduces no second preimage and no native H domain.

Native2SyntaxGrammarBundleV1.description: The installed, closure-bound grammar bundle that a syntax-only analysis parses with. It is the component that INTERPRETS a body span in that mode, so it is pinned exactly the way a toolchain is: closureId names an admitted kind=grammar closure, parserVersion must equal that closure manifest's semanticVersion (admission refuses native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest otherwise, mirroring the compiler-version rule), and bundleDigest is the exact retained bundle identity. `grammars` is the CLOSED bundled-grammar set: it is what native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' actually denotes, and what makes `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` decidable rather than a matter of taste.

parserName.description: The component that reads the body span. Not a compiler: a syntax-only universe executes none, and naming one here would claim an interpretation that never happened.

languageId.description: Every language the host actually bundles a grammar for, matching BUNDLED_GRAMMARS exactly. An earlier revision listed only typescript/javascript/rust and claimed equality with the body-language-version enum as a drift check; that could not express the four data/document grammars the host has always bundled, so native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' was unrepresentable for them. What is actually held equal to the body-language-version enum is the set of languages whose grammars are syntaxClass=code - see syntaxClass.

syntaxClass.description: Which capability this grammar's files bear, and the exact distinction the original contracts already draw. `code`: the language has the body spans native-evidence section 6.3 defines - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L1-L3 normalisation table, so its files can bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations. Its languageId MUST be a member of the foundation body-language-version languageId enum, because that identifier goes into the clone preimage. `data-document`: a bundled grammar for a data or document format with no such body spans and no published tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law anywhere in this kit. Its files are grammar-only members - accounted, never `unsupported-file` - and bear inventory evidence (file/package/vcs-change); they mint no body identity, and its languageId MUST NOT be in the body-language-version enum, since it can never appear in a clone preimage. Claiming code-construct syntax facts for a data format would require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, which is exactly the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to avoid.

normalizer.description: The clone normalisation component this bundle ships. It is recorded so the clones rung has a bound owner in syntax-only mode; it is deliberately NOT part of the body-language-version record, because the normalisation level specification is already its own framed component of the body identity.

Native2SyntaxNativeContextV2.description: The native context of the syntax-only language mode. It carries exactly the grammar bundle that interprets a body span and nothing else: no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no node_modules layout, no config graph. Those all belong to resolution, and a grammar-only analysis performs none. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would be asserting semantics the mode never computes.

Native2SyntaxUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.description: The universe of the syntax-only mode. Its identity is the admitted grammar context plus the SELECTED grammar set for this analysis: selecting a different grammar set is a different universe, exactly as selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is visible to every consumer rather than being an invisible default. It carries the constant resolutionAttempted=false so no consumer can read a syntax-only universe as a resolution claim: semantic rungs under it are language-tier-unsupported, not merely absent.

selectedGrammarIds.description: A subset of the context bundle's grammarIds. Admission refuses a selection naming a grammar the bundle does not contain; an empty selection is not expressible, because a universe that parsed nothing could not have produced a fact.

Native2TestResultsAdapterInputV1.description: INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was TestResultsPayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).

kind.description: Which recognized configuration file this node is. DERIVED from node.path by the closed table at #/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law, never asserted: exact case-sensitive basename `tsconfig.json` -> tsconfig, `jsconfig.json` -> jsconfig, every other basename -> other. The rule is total and applies to EVERY node, entry and non-entry alike. `other` is an ordinary value, not a defect: `tsconfig.build.json` reached as a base is `other`, and an explicitly selected custom-named configuration is an `other` ENTRY that still derives configOrigin tsconfig. This field is inside the hashed record, so the rule is an identity rule.

extendsResolved.description: The ORDERED resolved extends edges of this node, in the order the config declares them. TypeScript 5.0 supports multiple entries in `extends` and a LATER entry wins, so precedence is the array order and must be retained: an unordered set or a single edge cannot represent an ordinary modern configuration. Empty means this node extends nothing. Repeated edges are retained; this is a sequence, not a set.

Native2TypeScriptConfigGraphV1.description: The resolved tsconfig/jsconfig extends graph a TypeScript universe commits to. entryConfigPath is the SELECTED root config the program was opened with, null exactly when the configuration was synthesized; nodes is every config file actually read, strictly ascending and unique by path, each carrying its inventoried snapshot digest, its kind and its ORDERED resolved extends edges with later-wins precedence. configOrigin is derived from the ENTRY node kind, never from the whole set: a jsconfig.json that extends a shared base.json is a jsconfig program. Every node must be reachable from the entry, every edge must name another node, and the edge graph must be acyclic. tsconfigGraphHash is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record). A selected entry whose kind is other represents an explicitly selected custom-named TypeScript configuration and derives configOrigin tsconfig. Every node's `kind` is derived from its path by the closed exact-basename table at #/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law - entry and non-entry alike - and a node whose declared kind is not the derived one refuses.

configGraphPaths.description: every tsconfig/jsconfig file in the resolved extends graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under configOrigin=synthesized

Native2TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.description: The TypeScript counterpart of CargoConfigProjectionV2. Stripping an option is disclosed here; it is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else.

Native2TypeScriptHonoredOptionsV1.description: The closed subset of the resolved compilerOptions that changes program membership, module resolution or checking. Every value is the EFFECTIVE post-resolution value of the admitted tsconfig graph (or of SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1 under js-synthesized), never a raw file field.

component.description: Declaration-file BASENAME of a `.d.ts` member of the admitted stdlib closure tree, e.g. lib.es2022.d.ts - not a lib name and not a tree path. Native2TypeScriptModuleResolutionMode.description: The effective moduleResolution the admitted compiler applies. It changes which specifiers resolve, so it is a native-context field and a universe key.

Native2TypeScriptNativeContextV2.description: Closed native context for the typescript-v2 universe; H domain `native.context.typescript.v2`. It is NOT NativeContextV2, which is the Rust context (targetTriple/hostTriple/cargo resolver); a typescript-v2 universe whose nativeContextId was minted from a Rust descriptor is refused.

Native2TypeScriptToolClosureV1.description: Every executable the TypeScript adapter may select: the bundled compiler and the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure2 named by closureId. No PATH lookup, no system `node`, no NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/TS_NODE_* from the environment.

compilerVersion.description: the semanticVersion of the ADMITTED signed compiler closure manifest; never the output of an unverified `tsc --version`

typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot.description: identity-and-evidence section 3: the 64-hex SUFFIX of the closure2 identity of the admitted kind=stdlib closure, exactly as ToolchainIdentityV1.rustcDevLlvmDigest is the suffix of the kind=rust-dev-llvm closure. libSelection.description: The effective `lib` NAMES the resolved compilerOptions select (after target defaulting), sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the retained unfolded names. The mapping is one-directional: a component is never mapped back into a selected name, and this array is never re-spelled into file names. The folded name set must also equal the folded honoredOptions.lib set; a duplicate under fold refuses native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection.

Native2UnitIdentityV1.description: The closed PREIMAGE of a compilation unit identity, published here with its domain, codec and selector precisely so that unitId is not an opaque digest: any consumer can rebuild these four fields from the unit row that carries them and recompute the identity. A delimiter-joined label was the earlier draft and is WITHDRAWN - it was injective only by excluding # from markerPath, and a # in a repository directory is admissible under the canonical repository-path contract, so that recipe narrowed admitted paths to make a delimiter work. coverage.description: The ANSWER over the examined partition, and the second committed encoding of the section 4.1 claim-1 question `did we look at every subject?`. It is an IMPLICATION, never an equality. coverage=unknown constrains examinedExhaustive in NEITHER direction: a host may examine the committed partition exhaustively and still answer unknown because the evidence it needs is missing rather than unexamined (ambiguous or missing Rust compilation ownership, an undeclared or unservable capability, an unlisted source variant), and it may also answer unknown because the examination itself was cut short. Only the converse is impossible: complete over a partition the producer says it did not examine exhaustively asserts a totality the same record disclaims. RC-6 says nothing about resolutionCompleteness.state - enumeration completeness and RESOLUTION completeness are different claims, and RC-3's coverage=complete with state=incomplete over real unresolved edges stays lawful. It is total over every registered (relation, rung) pair including the twelve non-resolved ones, holds for a fact-free entry over an empty examined scope, and is enforced by coverage_bijection at the producer boundary (admit_coverage_result_v3) AND again at retained Run closure, whose disagreement is PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on the existing native.coverage-bijection-mismatch carrier - no new key and no new public detail.

INTERNAL unit root: the EMPTY STRING for the project root, otherwise a CanonicalRelativeDirV1. The external sentinel "." is NEVER a value of this field. "." is the EXTERNAL spelling only: Config2 discovery.workspaceRoots and CLI --workspace-root inbound (discovery-defaults.normalize_explicit_root, "." -> ""), and the outward workspaceRoot of the shared scope record and of enumeration cells (discovery-defaults.spell_root, "" -> "."), whose type is WorkspaceRootText and which states that it MAY be "." and is NOT LogicalPath. A retained WorkspaceUnitV2 carries the internal form and is never silently normalized after retention: _under_unit, _rel and the deepest-unit length ranking all read this field as an exact prefix. Segments are decided by SPLITTING ON "/" and testing EXACT equality, which is the decision procedure the house already implements identically in two independent places: foundation/identity-model.v3.py `ordered()` (rejects a leading "/", a backslash, a NUL and any segment in ["", ".", ".."] for every `path`/`logicalPath` string) and discovery-defaults.py `normalize_explicit_root()` (same four tests over `spec.split("/")`). The negative test is therefore attached PER SEGMENT and ends with a strict end-of-input assertion rather than "$": "$" also matches before a trailing newline, and a ".*"-prefixed lookahead does not cross a newline at all, so a single whole-string lookahead both accepts "a
/../b" (an exact ".." segment) and rejects "a/.
" (whose final segment is ".
", not "."). No character beyond "/", backslash and NUL is excluded, because the owning grammar excludes none: a literal newline or other non-dot character inside a segment stays admissible. The declarative at-most-255-characters-per-segment bound of #/$defs/LogicalPath is deliberately NOT imported here; identity-schemas.v3 records it as a different, explicitly non-equivalent enforcement that reaches only two Blob path fields, and neither `ordered()` nor `normalize_explicit_root` imposes it.
